title: A site page that frames a page of its own origin loads inside Tracy's preview: the comment picker's narrow frame-ancestors names 'self' beside the app origin
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-web/test/preview-ticket.test.mjs (the site proxy runs in-process against a stubbed upstream; nothing on the machine is touched)
S2: Read the ok/not ok line of each named test.
expect: A framed request carrying a valid continuation cookie (what a nested same-origin iframe sends) gets a second CSP that is exactly frame-ancestors 'self' <app origin>.
The site's own CSP stays a separate header, untouched.

selectors.header: the appended Content-Security-Policy on a picker answer

evidence: Measured 25/10/2026 on tracy-ai-8836f920.tracy.site (dev): the page frames /wp-content/themes/tracy/assets/demo/tracy-demo-edit.html; on the public site it loads, in Tracy's preview the nested frame showed 'refused to connect'. A headless Chromium loop (app -> site -> same-origin iframe) reproduces the block with 'frame-ancestors <app>' and loads with 'frame-ancestors 'self' <app>'.
fence: The proxy's response headers in-process. Not exercised by this case: a real browser on dev (measured separately after deploy).

tests: inject: the narrow frame-ancestors is a SEPARATE CSP header; the site policy is untouched
inject: the narrow frame-ancestors lets the site frame its own pages inside the app, nothing more
